# iPhone devicekey visitor history retrieval (2026-02-02 13:10Z)

_**User**_

@miataru/views/iPhone/Devices Views/iPhone_DeviceNavigationView.swift it seems that , when a devicekey is set for the current user device, it is not properly used during navigation to retrieve the visitor history. 

Analyze if this is the case, go ahead and analyze the project and all miataru client use for proper use of devicekey if the devicekey is set to avoid missing other cases like this

Miataru DeviceKey authentication plan (2026-01-31 13:59Z)\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":11,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"The Miataru server and all write requests through the Miataru client supports a DeviceKey. \\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":13,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"DeviceKey authentication provides secure, device-level authentication for location updates and sensitive operations. Each device can set a unique cryptographic key (up to 256 Unicode characters) that must be provided for protected operations.\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":16,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Device owners set an initial DeviceKey using the /v1/setDeviceKey endpoint\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":19,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"When a DeviceKey is set, protected endpoints require the key to be provided\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":22,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"DeviceKeys can be changed by providing the current key along with the new key\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":25,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"The following operations require DeviceKey authentication when a DeviceKey is set for the device:\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":37,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Initially (when a DeviceID is generated) the DeviceKey is empty and not set. The app should hold / persist the state whether the DeviceKey has been set or not in the past. It should store the actual DeviceKey as well as the date+time of when it was last changed/set. Preferably the UserDefaults store - alike current settings store - should be used.\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":39,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"When a device key has been set in app it should be used for all Miataru client operations that support the DeviceKey. When those functions are being called and the server returns an error (because server side error OR when the device key is false) the app should handle this properly (make a plan how to implement to handle it and document behavior).\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":41,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"As initially no user has configured a DeviceKey (e.g. its not set) we firstly need to implement a view to set/view/update the new DeviceKey:\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":45,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"If a DeviceKey is not set yet: State (A)\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":46,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"If a DeviceKey is set: State (B)\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":48,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"View state (A) No DeviceKey set yet:\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":49,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"When no DeviceKey is set yet there should be a text explaining the meaning of the device key and the current state of „not set“. You should come up with a good explanation text helping the user to understand what the device key does and how it is important (e.g. protects any data write operations etc.). When set once it cannot be removed, only set to a different/new DeviceKey. If it is lost somehow the DeviceID cannot be updated/restored/becomes unusable and needs to be reset to a new DeviceID.\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":51,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Below the explanation text there should be a button „generate and set DeviceKey“. When tapped the App should generate a UUID and use the MiataruClient to set this UUID as the new DeviceKey for the current device (setDeviceKey function). This new DeviceKey should properly persisted, including the current date/time.\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":55,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"View state (B) When a DeviceKey has been successfully set on the server the view shows:\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":56,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"- the current DeviceKey (textbox) + copy-to-clipboard icon+functionality\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":57,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"- the time/date of the last update of the DeviceKey\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":61,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"When the regenerate/reset button is tapped a new DeviceKey is generated. The Miataru Client setDeviceKey function is called with the OLD DeviceKey and the NEW DeviceKey. When this is successful the new DeviceKey is persisted (+ time/date of setting).\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":65,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"When the restore button is tapped a textbox entry opens with OK/cancel option. The user can paste / enter a previously saved DeviceKey from the clipboard or enter it with the keyboard. In order to check if the key is valid the app will try to call setDeviceKey with this user-provided-DeviceKey as the CurrentDeviceKey and NewDeviceKey. If it is valid the server will respond accordingly. If it is not, the server will also provide an error message and the app can handle this by showing the error message and re-opening the entry dialog with the previously user-entered-DeviceKey. The user can then either change the text and try again or cancel the process.\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":128,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"  \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"prompt\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Explore codebase to find where device settings/UserDefaults are stored (settings manager, device ID storage). This should surface the error on app launch when the 403 occurs.\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4196,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"when a location update  (foreground and background) fails because of a wrong devicekey (and only because of this) the app should stop updating/trying until its launched by the user again and the key has been reset to a working key. \\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4198,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"When the update fails because of the devicekey mismatch there is no dialog / sheet / message being displayed right now\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4207,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"I'm adding a deviceKeyAuthBlocked flag in SettingsManager set by LocationManager on auth errors to stop location updates until user relaunches and resets the key. I'll ensure LocationManager checks this flag before sending updates and clears it on app activation if the key changes, persisting the flag in UserDefaults. Banner display will trigger only when active, and error handling will update tracking and server status accordingly.\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4210,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"I'm implementing deviceKeyAuthBlocked and deviceKeyAuthBlockedKey in SettingsManager to track auth errors and block updates until the device key resets on app launch. LocationManager will stop tracking on block, skip sending updates while blocked, and auto-restart tracking on app activation if unblocked and user preferences allow. Banner display triggers on app launch if blocked. The block guards startTracking and observing settings to prevent unwanted updates while blocked.&lt;/details&gt;&lt;/think&gt;\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4495,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Made the DeviceKey mismatch stop all location updates until the app is relaunched **and** the key is changed to a working one, and ensured the user sees a banner message on app launch.\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4498,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"- **Stop updates on mismatch**: When UpdateLocation fails due to DeviceKey mismatch, tracking stops and a &#96;deviceKeyAuthBlocked&#96; flag is persisted.\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4500,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"- **Auto-resume after key reset**: Changing the DeviceKey clears the block; when the app becomes active, tracking restarts if allowed.\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4509,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"is deviceKeyAuthBlocked reset when key is restored/set and working again?\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4516,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"**Clarifying deviceKey reset logic**\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4518,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"The deviceKey resets only if deviceKeyAuthBlocked is true, a blocked key exists, and the current key differs from the blocked key, ensuring same keys don't clear. If a restored key differs, reset happens to handle mismatch between client and server keys.&lt;/details&gt;&lt;/think&gt;\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4522,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Yes, it’s reset when the key changes to a different value. In &#96;SettingsManager.deviceKey&#96;’s &#96;didSet&#96;, if &#96;deviceKeyAuthBlocked&#96; is true **and** the new key differs from the blocked key, the block is cleared and the blocked key is removed. The app should hold / persist the state whether the DeviceKey has been set or not in the past. It should store the actual DeviceKey as well as the date+time of when it was last changed/set.\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":39,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"When a device key has been set in app it should be used for all Miataru client operations that support the DeviceKey. When set once it cannot be removed, only set to a different/new DeviceKey. If it is lost somehow the DeviceID cannot be updated/restored/becomes unusable and needs to be reset to a new DeviceID.\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":51,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Below the explanation text there should be a button „generate and set DeviceKey“. This new DeviceKey should properly persisted, including the current date/time.\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":55,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"View state (B) When a DeviceKey has been successfully set on the server the view shows:\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":56,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"- the current DeviceKey (textbox) + copy-to-clipboard icon+functionality\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":57,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"- the time/date of the last update of the DeviceKey\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":61,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"When the regenerate/reset button is tapped a new DeviceKey is generated. The Miataru Client setDeviceKey function is called with the OLD DeviceKey and the NEW DeviceKey. When this is successful the new DeviceKey is persisted (+ time/date of setting).\\\\\\\"},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":65,\\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"When the restore button is tapped a textbox entry opens with OK/cancel option. The user can paste / enter a previously saved DeviceKey from the clipboard or enter it with the keyboard. In order to check if the key is valid the app will try to call setDeviceKey with this user-provided-DeviceKey as the CurrentDeviceKey and NewDeviceKey. If it is valid the server will respond accordingly. If it is not, the server will also provide an error message and the app can handle this by showing the error message and re-opening the entry dialog with the previously user-entered-DeviceKey.
